deploy-bot: [DEPLOY CHECK] release/rc-42 -> prod: SBOM provenance mismatch detected for image registry.redwood.com/runtime:sha256:ef12f9...
deploy-bot: Vulnerability scan: 1 moderate (CVE-2025-1234) in transitive dep 'fastjson'. Canary halted. /cc @security @anita :warning:

maya: Thanks — what's the exact provenance mismatch? can we pin to previous digest or rerun SBOM after rebuild?

zach: SBOM shows base_image_id != release metadata. Build picked up a new base snapshot. Quick options: (1) pin to last-known-good digest `sha256:abcde12345` (2) rebuild with pinned base and re-run SBOM (preferred) (3) security exception (last resort). I can push a rebuild if we want to stay in change window.

anita: Change window ends in ~45m. We can't block much longer. What's the risk if we resume a tiny canary (1%) and hold full rollout?

sam: Canary at 1% is acceptable. Deploybot currently halted canary. We can resume with `deploybot resume --canary=1% --hold-full=true` and enable auto-rollback on error. Note: security will still require SBOM baseline for compliance. :eyes:

maya: If we pin base image digest, will that satisfy SBOM provenance checks? need confirmation from security.

zach: Pinning makes provenance stable; SBOM should match expected source and include provenance token. Snippet of regenerated SBOM: 
```sbom
name: runtime
image: registry.redwood.com/runtime@sha256:abcde12345
base: debian-12.1
provenance: git+https://git.redwood/repo@refs/tags/v1.2.3
```
I'll open a PR to update the image ref and trigger a rebuild.

security-bot: /cc @sec-team please review: SBOM provenance mismatch + CVE-2025-1234. Recommended mitigation: short-term pin + rebuild. Requesting expedited review for canary exception. :warning:

anita: Legal looped in? If not, ping legal. We can approve a canary-only exception with compensating controls (detailed logs, alerts, 30m manual review).

zach: I can create a canary-scoped exception: `gatectl create-exception --cve CVE-2025-1234 --scope=canary --expires=3h --mitigation='rebuild-with-pinned-base'` — shall I proceed?

deploy-bot: action required: gatectl exception pending (owner: zach). Canary remains halted until security accepts exception. Use `deploybot resume` after approval.

legal-bot: Notified legal@redwood.com — please attach SBOM diff + mitigation plan in the ticket. If legal approves licensing risk, tag with `legal:approved`.

maya: I'll draft the SBOM diff and attach build logs. If security grants quick exception we can canary and schedule rollback if anything abnormal.

sam: Ops note: if canary proceeds, enable verbose tracing and token-level cost logs so we can detect regressions quickly. Set canary to 1% for 60 minutes then manual decision.

zach: PR #3145 created: updates image ref and triggers rebuild. SBOM regenerated. Link: https://git.redwood/repo/pulls/3145 :thumbsup:

security-bot: Sec-OK pending manual review. @zach include SBOM provenance artifact and full build log (sha256) in the PR for faster sign-off.

anita: I'll approve the canary-only rollout once security gives green. @sec-team please expedite — change window closing.

maya: Thanks. Looping in @deploy-oncall in case canary needs immediate rollback outside core hours.

sam: Final ops checklist if exception granted: 1) resume canary at 1% 2) enable auto-rollback on error 3) monitor SLOs + error budget closely 4) revert image to previous digest if any regression.

zach: Executing follow-ups now — building pinned image, pushing provenance artifact. Will post updates here when gatectl exception is created.
